key_insight: This paper turns 3D boxes from a vague hint into a precise editing instruction. By specifying both the starting and ending boxes, users can control large spatial changes in real-image editing more reliably.
problem_solved: Existing text prompts and 2D conditioning are often ambiguous for edits involving big object movement or camera/viewpoint changes. The paper addresses the lack of a clear geometric control signal for these kinds of transformations.
method: Represent the edit as a pair of 3D bounding boxes: the input box and the output box.
Use these boxes as a structured specification for the desired transformation, rather than as loose location hints.
Reformulate image editing as a well-posed geometry-driven problem, enabling more controllable spatial edits in real images.
impact: For practitioners, this offers a more interpretable and controllable way to perform complex image edits, especially when spatial precision matters. It can improve reliability in workflows involving object relocation, pose changes, or viewpoint edits.

paper_title: Thinking in Boxes: 3D Editing in Real Images Made Easy
paper_authors: Pradhaan S Bhat, Naveen Chandra R, Rishubh Parihar, Vaibhav Vavilala, R. Venkatesh Babu
